rationale: The change is small, focused, and correct. It converts LangfuseLiteLLMErrorOutputCallback from a module-level singleton to a per-request instance so the user's query is available when a guardrail rejects an LLM call. The singleton carried no state, so the behavioural change is purely additive: traces that were previously blank on guardrail rejection now receive both input (the user query) and output (the classified error message). The user_input is passed through the existing set_current_trace_io / update_current_trace path, which already handles PII in the same way as all other Langfuse traces — no new data exfiltration surface is introduced. Removal of the module-level singleton eliminates a shared-mutable reference that would have been a threading hazard had state ever been added. The new test exercises the full on_llm_error path with a known user_input and asserts the trace_io call receives both keyword arguments. The existing singleton-identity assertion in TestGetRunConfigLangfuseCallbacks is correctly relaxed to isinstance. Quality gates: 189 sanity tests passed (uvx codemie-test-harness run --marks 'api and sanity' -n 4 --reruns 3), ruff clean, license-check clean.
